UN votes to adopt new world map that shows Africa’s true scale 聯合國表決採用新世界地圖   真實呈現非洲面積
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:44:22 UTC
01:44:22 KST

The UN has voted to adopt a resolution for the world to formally phase out the traditional Mercator map of the globe in favor of one that more accurately displays Africa’s size.
In a session at its headquarters in New York, the UN general assembly officially retired the 16th-century Mercator projection in favor of one based on the more accurate 2018 Equal Earth design.
At the session, 164 countries voted in favor of the resolution. Only the US voted against it while six other countries — Serbia, Estonia, Georgia, Lithuania, Moldova and Ukraine — abstained.
Photo: AFP 照片：法新社
UN resolutions are non-enforceable, so countries and institutions will not be mandated to use only the new projection or forbidden from using the old one. However, the outcome is expected to result in an update of classroom curriculums and everyday technology given the wide usage of the Mercator projection in education, technology and governance.
Togo, which spearheaded a campaign for the resolution on behalf of the African Union (AU), said the resolution “recognizes and affirms that disproportionate cartographic representations, particularly those resulting from the Mercator projection, have had lasting cognitive, educational, cultural, geopolitical and socioeconomic effects, contributing to a drastic reduction in the perceived size of Africa and other regions of the world in the global collective imagination.”
Speaking before the resolution passed, Robert Dussey, Togo’s foreign affairs minister, said: “This discussion is not a political discussion [but] a scientific discussion, because there is scientific proof so we all have to accept the reality.”
Photo: Stefan Kühn /Wikimedia Commons 照片：Stefan Kühn∕維基共享資源
The Mercator layout was introduced by the Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator in 1569 to help sailors navigate the seas. Almost five centuries later, it remains the global standard.
Because of its projection style, however, regions near the equator appear significantly smaller than they are, whereas high-latitude areas look much larger. For example, the map shows Africa as being similar in size to Greenland, but the continent is 14 times larger than the Danish territory.
“You could fit the United States, China, India, Japan, Mexico and much of Europe into Africa and still have land to spare,” says a petition on Change.org for the #CorrectTheMap campaign, which has more than 11,000 signatures. The AU endorsed the campaign in August of last year and then asked Togo to spearhead its adoption.
On Sept. 4, before the vote, France’s foreign minister Jean-Noel Barrot spoke in support of the resolution. “[We] will abandon the Mercator projection in favor of map representations tailored to specific uses, more faithful to actual surface areas and in line with the recommendations of cartographers and scientists,” Barrot said during a speech at the Sorbonne University in Paris, in a move seen as part of France’s push to increase goodwill among its former colonies. France will now use the Eckert IV projection, which is close to the Equal Earth projection recommended in the resolution.
Historians and geographers have said for years that the Mercator projection is rooted in western stereotypes. Activists have echoed this, with some coining the term “cartographic colonialism.”
Some argue that the map has subtly shaped international power dynamics by minimizing the physical presence of the global south and visually inflating northern hemisphere nations while shrinking equatorial regions. This is said to have reinforced systemic biases in international trade, development priorities and educational frameworks.
One of the Mercator projection’s most prominent critics was Arno Peters, a German historian, who launched the Peters world map based on the Gall–Peters projection in 1973. It has often been used as an alternative to the Mercator map.
Togo’s #CorrectTheMap campaign promoted the use of the 2018 Equal Earth design, which was developed by an international team of cartographers. Supporters say it will help to reverse perceptions of Africa and decolonize global curriculums.
(The Guardian)
聯合國通過一項決議，正式支持全球逐步淘汰以「麥卡托投影法」（Mercator projection）製作的傳統世界地圖，改用能更準確呈現非洲實際面積的地圖投影法。
聯合國大會在紐約總部舉行會議，正式支持以2018年推出、準確度更高的「平等地球投影」（Equal Earth projection）為基礎的地圖，取代16世紀的麥卡托投影。
這項表決有164個國家投下贊成票。只有美國投下反對票，另外有6個國家——塞爾維亞、愛沙尼亞、喬治亞、立陶宛、摩爾多瓦與烏克蘭——棄權。
聯合國決議並不具法律強制力，因此各國及各機構不會被強制要求只能使用新投影法，也不會被禁止繼續使用舊地圖。不過，由於麥卡托投影法長期廣泛應用於教育、科技與政府治理，此次決議預料將促使學校課程及日常科技產品逐步更新。
代表「非洲聯盟」（African Union）推動這項決議的多哥表示，這項決議「承認並闡明，不成比例的地圖呈現方式，尤其是麥卡托投影法所造成的結果，已造成長久的認知、教育、文化、地緣政治與社會經濟影響，使非洲及世界其他地區的實際大小在全球集體想像中遭到大幅縮減」。
在決議通過前，多哥外交部長羅伯特．杜西表示：「這不是政治問題，而是科學問題，因為有科學證據，所以我們都必須接受這個事實」。
1569年，佛蘭芒製圖師格拉杜斯．麥卡托發明了麥卡托投影法，原本是為了協助水手在海上航行。近五個世紀過去了，它仍然是全球標準。
然而，由於這種投影方式的特性，靠近赤道的地區在地圖上會顯得比實際面積小得多，而高緯度地區則會被大幅放大。例如，麥卡托地圖上的非洲看起來跟格陵蘭島差不多大，但實際上，非洲大陸的面積是格陵蘭這丹麥自治領地的14倍。
線上公眾請願與連署平台Change.org上一份支持#CorrectTheMap（修正地圖）運動的請願書指出：「你可以把美國、中國、印度、日本、墨西哥，以及歐洲大部分地區都放進非洲這塊土地，還有得剩」。這份請願書目前已有超過1.1萬人連署。非洲聯盟在2025年8月正式支持這項運動，並要求多哥帶頭推動各國採用新的地圖投影法。
在9月4日表決前，法國外交部長也發言支持這項決議。法國外長尚．諾埃爾．巴羅在巴黎索邦大學演講時表示：「我們將放棄麥卡托投影法，改用依不同用途設計的地圖呈現方式；這些方式更忠於實際地表面積，也符合製圖師與科學家的建議」。外界認為，此舉也是法國試圖向其前殖民地釋出善意、改進關係的一環。法國之後將採用艾克特第四投影法（Eckert IV projection），其特性與決議中推薦的等積地球投影相近。
歷史學家與地理學家多年來不斷指出，麥卡托投影法帶有西方中心主義的歷史與刻板印象。社運人士也提出類似批評，有人還提出了「地圖學殖民主義」（cartographic colonialism）一詞。
部分學者認為，麥卡托投影地圖在不知不覺間形塑了國際權力關係：它縮小了全球南方在視覺上的存在感，卻放大了北半球國家的視覺比例，同時縮小赤道地區。這種視覺上的偏差，被認為進一步強化了國際貿易、發展政策優先順序及教育體系中的結構性偏見。
麥卡托投影法最著名的批評者之一，是德國歷史學家阿諾．彼得斯。他在1973年推出以高爾—彼德斯投影法（Gall–Peters projection）為基礎的彼得斯世界地圖，被視為麥卡托地圖的一種替代方案。
多哥主導的#CorrectTheMap運動則推廣2018年推出的「平等地球投影」。這套設計由一支國際製圖師團隊共同開發。支持者認為，新投影法有助於扭轉人們對非洲的既有認知，並推動全球教育課程的去殖民化。
（台北時報林俐凱編譯）

Health center head fined for giving out weight-loss drugs
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:44:20 UTC
01:44:20 KST

The head of a public health center in Tainan has been fined NT$100,000 for allegedly purchasing injectable GLP-1 drugs for weight loss and privately supplying them to people without a prescription.
An audit by the Tainan Public Health Bureau found that the Sinhua District (新化) Health Station had purchased 780 doses of injectable GLP-1 drugs, but only five doses were in inventory.
It was unable to provide the corresponding doctor’s prescription and usage records of the missing doses.
Photo: Wu Liang-yi, Taipei Times
Station director Wu Cheng-ta (吳政達) yesterday admitted that he purchased the drugs and provided them to his friends and relatives, adding that he sold them at cost without making any profit.
Wu said he has acknowledged his mistake, and that his behavior lacked thorough consideration.
Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Division of Medicinal Products senior specialist Liu Chia-ping (劉佳萍) called for the government to tighten oversight of the distribution and use of GLP-1 drugs, adding that the agency has collaborated with local health bureaus since 2024 to conduct special audits.
Starting in October last year, GLP-1 drugs were included into a drug traceability tracking and management system, requiring pharmaceutical companies to report monthly drug distribution data, she said.
The FDA this year expanded the scope of the audit by analyzing drug reporting data to identify abnormal distribution patterns, Liu said.
The agency has provided records to local health bureaus for further investigation, including the Sinhua District Health Station, she added.
While GLP-1s have gained wide public attention for their use in weight loss, the drugs cannot be purchased or used as over-the-counter products, the FDA said.
People seeking to lose weight should see a doctor for professional evaluation, and should only use drugs according to medical instructions, it said.
The FDA urged people not to acquire GLP-1s through relatives, friends, online platforms or other illegal channels, and avoid administering it on their own.
The agency would continue to monitor the supply of GLP-1s through drug traceability and reporting systems, it said, adding that any illegal supply or usage would be investigated and penalized according to the law.

Turkish police on Sunday swooped on gay bars and the homes of LGBTQ activists, arresting at least 60 people in raids authorities said were aimed at boosting traditional family values, officials and activists said.
Turkey’s LGBTQ community has frequently been targeted by the government, with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan lashing it as a “deviant movement” of “perverts” responsible for the falling birthrate.
Sunday’s raid came a day after the accounts of more than a dozen Turkish LGBTQ organizations were blocked on X at the request of the authorities, a watchdog said.
Photo: Demiroren News Agency via AFP
“As part of the ‘My Family is Safe’ operations ... carried out in collaboration with our police and gendarmerie forces, legal proceedings have been initiated against 162 suspects, 9 organizations and 13 companies in ... a total of 15 provinces,” Turkish Minister of Justice Akin Gurlek posted on social media. Many were around Istanbul and Ankara.
Gurlek said the raids were part of the “Decade of the Family” proclaimed by Erdogan, aimed at “protecting our children, the institution of the family and social order.”
At least 63 people were detained, the Turkish state’s Anadolu Agency reported.
LGBTQ and women’s rights activists form one of the main centers of resistance to the Islamist-rooted conservative government in power since 2002.
In Istanbul, police raided several gay bars and a nightclub regarded as a haven for the LGBTQ community, video footage from pro-government media showed.
Also targeted was a men’s hammam reputed to be a venue for prostitution.
LGBTQ rights organisation Kaos GL, whose offices were searched and whose leaders were taken into custody, earlier said that “nearly 50 defenders of the rights of LGBTQ people ... have been taken into custody or are subject to legal proceedings involving interrogations or detentions” across the country.
Judicial authorities in Ankara had alleged that Kaos GL made “posts containing obscenity” on its Web site and social media channels, and that the content was accessible to children, the group said.
While same-sex relations are not a criminal offense in Turkey, homophobia is widespread.
The European Parliament’s rapporteur on Turkey condemned the arrests as “a shocking escalation in the repression” in the country. Turkey’s efforts to join the EU have been frozen in the past few years, but it remains a key trade and political partner.

Russian Convoy Resupplies Syrian Coastal Facilities for First Time Since Moscow-Damascus Deal
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:43:00 UTC
01:43:00 KST

A convoy of Russian naval and cargo vessels delivered supplies last week to Syrian coastal facilities long used by Moscow’s military, two sources familiar with the operation said, in the first such mission since Damascus and Moscow agreed last month on the future of Russia’s military presence in the country.
The operation offers an early indication that Moscow is continuing to resupply facilities at Tartus port and the Khmeimim airbase under the new deal, which provides for civilian facilities used by Russia to be transferred to Syrian control and military sites to be turned into joint training centers.
Russian forces are to remain at the bases under the agreement. Russia has used Khmeimim and Tartus to project power across the Mediterranean, Middle East and Africa. Tartus provides Moscow with its only naval repair and replenishment facility in the Mediterranean.
Moscow has supplied both sites in recent months but last week's was the first since the Aug. 9 agreement was announced.
The four-vessel convoy arrived at the Mediterranean port of Tartus on Sept. 7, according to movements tracked by Reuters and maritime intelligence firm SynMax.
Satellite imagery verified by Reuters showed the Russian Ro-Ro cargo ship Sparta and navy replenishment oiler Akademik Pashin docked on Sept. 8 in Tartus at piers 3 and 4, respectively.
A Reuters reporter saw the two vessels docked there on Sept. 9, while Russian tanker General Skobelev remained offshore. A surveillance balloon was seen flying over the port during the unloading operation.
A Syrian military source and a Russian-Syrian businessman familiar with the operation said Sparta unloaded supplies including ammunition destined for Khmeimim and Tartus. Reuters could not independently confirm the contents of the shipment or their intended recipients.
SynMax identified the fourth vessel in the convoy as Admiral Levchenko, a Russian Udaloy-class destroyer.
Syria’s General Authority of Ports and Customs and Russia's embassy in Damascus did not respond to requests for comment.
Vessels sailed dark
The vessels stopped transmitting their signal shortly after crossing Strait of Gibraltar towards the Mediterranean. Reuters tracked the group via satellite imagery as it continued east and ultimately reached the Syrian coast.
Sparta has long been used in Russian military logistics in Syria and is under U.S. sanctions. General Skobelev is also under Western sanctions over transporting Russian oil.
Damascus and Moscow reached the agreement over Khmeimim and Tartus after 18 months of negotiations following the December 2024 overthrow of former President Bashar al-Assad, a close Russian ally.

German intelligence report warns of rising Chinese, Russian spy threat
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:41:44 UTC
01:41:44 KST

German intelligence report warns of rising Chinese, Russian spy threat
A report by Germany’s counter-intelligence agency said some surveillance activities targeting military infrastructure can be linked to China
Germany’s military counter-intelligence agency, known as MAD, has warned of a growing threat from hybrid attacks and the use of recruited contract agents, or low-level agents, saying Germany is a “prioritised target of Russian espionage activities”.
According to the agency’s annual report released on Monday, it cited Germany’s geostrategic position in Europe and Nato the expansion of the Bundeswehr and the introduction of new weapons systems as reasons for the heightened targeting.
“The hybrid threat situation in Germany has continued to deteriorate,” MAD says. These include cyberattacks, drone attacks, attempts at political influence, and disruptive attacks targeting transport, energy facilities and telecommunications.
MAD said the potential threat of sabotage by low-level agents has also increased significantly. The report does not provide comparative figures, which could lead adversaries to draw conclusions from the data.

Macklemore: ‘Free Palestine’ cost me my place on Ed Sheeran tour
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:40:11 UTC
01:40:11 KST

Breadcrumb
Macklemore after Ed Sheeran tour removal: 'I am not a victim. Palestinians are'
Macklemore has hit back after being removed from the remainder of Ed Sheeran’s US tour, saying “the victims are the Palestinian people” as he defended his support for Palestinian liberation.
In a statement posted on social media, the US rapper said his support for Palestine had become “too much of a risk” after he was given a platform at some of America’s biggest stadiums.
“I am not a victim. Ed Sheeran is not a victim. Pink is not a victim. We have careers, money, opportunities, safety, and audiences around the world. Whatever consequences any of us face for what we say, we get to go home to our families," he said. "The victims are the Palestinian people. The men, women and children who have been killed, starved, displaced and forced to live through unimaginable violence.”
He said there was “no neutral position between the oppressor and the oppressed”, arguing that the consequences faced by artists who speak out could not compare with the suffering of Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.
“When one side has the bombs and bottomless financial and military support from America, refusing to take a side doesn’t leave you in the middle,” he said.
Macklemore said he had been told by Sheeran that Robert Kraft, a staunchly pro-Israel billionaire whose company owns Gillette Stadium, had objected to him performing at the venue after his “Free Palestine” remarks at MetLife Stadium.
He said Sheeran had also told him that Kraft rallied other stadium owners, who warned the singer they would not allow him to perform at their venues if Macklemore remained on the tour.
Messina Touring Group, the promoter of Sheeran’s US Loop tour, later confirmed that venues had said they would not allow concerts with Macklemore on the lineup, saying this could have led to the tour being cancelled and affected hundreds of thousands of fans.
Macklemore was subsequently removed from the remaining support dates.
The rapper said the decision came despite his 13-year friendship with Sheeran, whom he described as a “brother”.
But he said their friendship could not override his responsibility to speak about Palestinians.
Macklemore said taking a position on Palestine could cost artists money, sponsorships, festivals, private shows, relationships and access.
‘Free Palestine’ became too much of a risk
Macklemore said he had called for Palestinian freedom on stages around the world for almost three years, but argued that performing alongside Sheeran at huge US stadiums had changed the stakes.
“At a certain level of exposure, ‘Free Palestine’ becomes too much of a risk,” he said.
“If I kept doing the shows, saying Free Palestine, with Ed implicitly supporting it, the crowd getting loud and showing undeniable support for Palestinian liberation, what artist might speak out next?
“The stage becomes resistance. Maybe that’s why this time it became so important to silence me.”
Macklemore performed at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium on 4 and 5 September, calling for a “Free Palestine” and telling the audience that Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank had not been forgotten.
He also performed his protest song Hind’s Hall alongside imagery depicting devastation in Gaza.
The performances prompted a petition from the pro-Israel lobby group the Israeli-American Council calling for his removal from the tour.
Criticism of Israel is not hatred of Jewish people
Macklemore also rejected attempts to portray his support for Palestine as hostility towards Jewish people.
He said accusations of antisemitism were being used to shield Israel from criticism, arguing that opposition to Israel and Zionism should not be conflated with hatred of Jewish people.
“Antisemitism is real. And that is exactly why the word matters too much to be used as a shield against criticism of the Israeli state,” he said.
“When criticizing Israel, opposing Zionism or saying ‘Free Palestine’ gets conflated with hatred of Jewish people, it doesn’t protect Jewish people. It protects Israel from accountability.”
At his second MetLife performance, Macklemore addressed Jewish members of the audience, saying criticism of Israel, apartheid and genocide was not criticism of them.
“My message is for peace, love; for all human beings to be treated with dignity, respect and equality,” he said.
He said the focus on his cancellation was insignificant compared with Palestinian suffering.
“Who is winning the internet, who is getting canceled, who gets to play the stadium and who doesn’t, all of it becomes so small when held against what we are actually witnessing in Gaza and the West Bank,” he said.
He said Palestinians were being “displaced, starved and killed” while public debate focused on which words artists were allowed to use.
‘I needed two’
Macklemore said he did not expect praise for speaking about Palestine, describing it instead as a responsibility.
Referencing the Arabic phrase “la shukra ala wajeb”, meaning there is no thanks for a duty, he said supporting Palestinians had become a duty for him and millions of others.
“That’s what this has become for me and millions of others around the world. A duty. Not something deserving of praise or gratitude. Not brave. Human.”
He said he did not need the full run of shows with Sheeran.
“I didn’t need 10 shows from Ed. I needed 2,” he said. “Two chances to stand in front of 90,000 people and say the words that somehow became too dangerous to say. Free Palestine.”
Macklemore said losing his place on the tour could ultimately help redirect attention towards Palestine.
“But if those words cost me the stage, while turning the conversation back to Palestine, then it was the most successful tour I’ve ever been on.”
Despite the fallout, Macklemore said he hoped his friendship with Sheeran could survive their disagreement.
“Thirteen years of friendship doesn’t disappear because of one painful disagreement,” he said.
He added that he hoped they would continue discussing “what neutrality means in a moment like this”.
“My door will always be open to continuing that conversation,” he said.

Nobel winner Parisi highlights need for more AI public research
Italy
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
18:38:23 CEST
01:38:23 KST

Italian Nobel Prize winning physicist
Giorgio Paris on Monday told ANSA there should be much more
publicly funded research into Artificial Intelligence (AI) amid
warnings from some of  its makers that it could wipe out
humanity in a few years' time - an "alarmist" scenario he
downplayed.
                                    
                                       
				The debate on the potentially deadly effects of AI sparked by
private companies including OpenAI "reinforces the need for a
public research centre" on the subject, the 2021 Nobel laureate
told ANSA.
                                    
                                       
				"It is a rather confused situation" involving a multitude of
variables, "but the danger of AI models evolving uncontrollably
seems something we can rule out," he observed.
                                    
                                       
				Alongside the proposal for a European public AI research
center—which Parisi recently presented to the Accademia dei
Lincei, of which he is a member—the Nobel laureate believes that
laws tailored to this new reality are needed and that now is the
time to consider the potential impact on employment and
education.
                                    
                                       
				The ongoing debate on AI is, however, "muddled," and "the first
thing that stands out is that all this cutting-edge research is
being conducted by private industry; consequently, we only have
the information that companies choose to release. It is hard to
say what is actually happening because there is much we do not
know."
While noting that he is not an expert on Large Language Models,
Parisi observed that "the danger of them evolving on their own
and without control seems highly unlikely" because "models must
be programmed."
Rome-born Parisi, 78, was awarded the 2021 Nobel Prize in
Physics jointly with Klaus Hasselmann and Syukuro Manabe for
groundbreaking contributions to theory of complex systems, in
particular "for the discovery of the interplay of disorder and
fluctuations in physical systems from atomic to planetary
scales".
                                    
                                       
				United States President Donald Trump on Monday also pooh-poohed
the warnings about AI's potential existential threat and said
the US was leading progress in the field and should not "kill
the goose that laid the golden egg".

UN warns Sudan aid system could 'collapse within weeks' without funding
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:38:12 UTC
01:38:12 KST

The United Nations has warned that a key logistics system delivering humanitarian aid to war-torn Sudan could collapse within weeks unless it receives urgent funding.
“The entire humanitarian system could collapse within weeks if we don't act now,” International Organization for Migration (IOM) chief Amy Pope said on Monday.
The war between Sudan’s army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which began in April 2023, has killed more than 200,000 people, according to aid workers.
The conflict triggered world’s current largest hunger and displacement crisis.
Aid pipeline is in crisis
The IOM said its Common Humanitarian Pipeline enables more than 100 national and international non-governmental organisations to deliver shelter and other essential non-food supplies across Sudan.
Since the war began, the system has reached 2.84 million people. However, its reach has declined as funding has fallen, despite humanitarian needs remaining at record levels.
The pipeline assisted more than one million people in 2024. So far in 2026, only 330,000 people have received support, including shelter and emergency household kits, through the system, the IOM said.
“Without immediate donor support, current shelter, sanitation and emergency household relief items are expected to be depleted by the end of September,” the UN agency said in a statement.
It added that the warehousing and operational capacity needed to keep the pipeline running could be sustained only until December 2026.
The IOM said it needed $15 million to maintain the pipeline at its minimum 2026 capacity for the next 12 months. Restoring operations to 2024 levels would require $42 million, it added.
The agency warned that reduced access to shelter would increase exposure to severe weather, disease and insecurity, while heightening the risks of gender-based violence, family separation and eviction in overcrowded displacement sites.
“Shelter is the foundation from which protection, health and recovery can begin,” Pope said. “When the pipeline stops, it is not simply warehouses that become empty. The entire humanitarian response becomes harder to deliver.”

7 points qu’Ursula von der Leyen abordera dans son discours sur l’état de l’Union
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:34:35 UTC
01:34:35 KST

BRUXELLES — Ursula von der Leyen a fait de l’indépendance de l’Europe face à un monde dangereux le pilier de son héritage politique. Mercredi, la présidente de la Commission européenne devra faire le point sur l’état d’avancement de cette ambition, et dévoiler les prochaines étapes.
Alors que l’UE est confrontée à des guerres, des feux de forêt et Donald Trump, Ursula von der Leyen profitera de son sixième discours sur l’état de l’Union pour présenter son programme : rendre l’Europe résiliente face au changement climatique ; tenir la cadence face à la Chine et des Etats-Unis en matière d’intelligence artificielle ; booster l’industrie de la défense européenne ; et réformer ses règles en matière d’immigration.
Le discours sera revu et réécrit jusqu’au moment même où elle le prononcera. Mais d’après des entretiens menés avec plus d’une douzaine de responsables européens, qui ont souhaité garder l’anonymat pour évoquer les priorités et les axes de discussion de la présidente, voici ce que la rédaction de POLITICO a appris sur le contenu de son intervention.
Advertisement
Intelligence artificielle
L’IA a été au cœur du séminaire de rentrée organisé par la Commission à Tervuren, près de Bruxelles, début septembre, lors duquel le discours a été préparé. Il est révélateur que le conseiller spécial de l’exécutif européen pour les applications industrielles de l’IA, le président de Siemens Jim Hagemann Snabe, ait été présent ce jour-là.
Lors d’une réunion distincte des directeurs de cabinet — au cours de laquelle ils ont présenté à Bjoern Seibert, le bras droit de von der Leyen, les priorités de leurs services à inclure dans le discours —, la question de la manière de présenter l’impact de l’IA sur l’emploi a été abordée.
L’équipe d’Ursula von der Leyen a demandé aux services compétents de la Commission de fournir, en vue du discours, de nouvelles statistiques sur le nombre d’emplois susceptibles d’être supprimés et créés à mesure que l’adoption de l’IA se généralise, selon l’un des responsables au fait des discussions.
Compétitivité
Deux ans après la publication du rapport de l’ancien Premier ministre italien Mario Draghi sur les moyens de redonner sa compétitivité au continent, Ursula von der Leyen s’apprête à dresser le bilan des efforts déployés par sa Commission pour remédier au marasme économique de l’Europe par la simplification administrative.
Elle devrait évoquer un “grand nettoyage en profondeur” de la réglementation et le principe de “simplicité dès la conception”, glisse un haut responsable européen. “Honnêtement, elle doit se montrer à la hauteur”, ajoute-t-il.
Toutefois, le même souligne que la compétitivité ne sera pas le thème principal du discours cette fois-ci. Cet honneur reviendra au…
Advertisement
Climat
Alors que l’Europe sort d’un été infernal, marqué par l’assèchement de ses fleuves et les feux de forêt, l’adaptation au changement climatique — l’un des principaux thèmes abordés par les commissaires européens lors du séminaire de rentrée — devrait occuper une place prépondérante dans son allocution.
L’exécutif européen travaille déjà à l’élaboration d’un plan visant à renforcer la résilience du continent face au changement climatique. Ce paquet de mesures — prévu pour fin octobre et qui devrait inclure, entre autres, un scénario climatique commun décrivant les conditions futures auxquelles les pays de l’UE devront se préparer, ainsi que des évaluations régulières des risques — sera probablement évoqué dans le discours. Reste à savoir à quel point la présidente entrera dans les détails.
Cette focalisation sur le climat intervient alors que la Commission de von der Leyen s’efforce de défendre son objectif de réduction des émissions de gaz à effet de serre à l’horizon 2040, tout en faisant face à la pression croissante des acteurs économiques et des gouvernements nationaux pour limiter le coût de la transition écologique.
Des pompiers luttent contre un incendie de forêt à Muğla, en Turquie, le 2 août 2021. | Yasin Akgul/AFP via Getty Images
Le commissaire chargé du Climat, Wopke Hoekstra, a fait détaillé à POLITICO que la Commission souhaitait s’assurer que la planification soit “intégrée” dans l’ensemble du processus d’élaboration des politiques européennes et nationales, ce qui signifie que la résilience climatique serait prise en compte à chaque étape du processus décisionnel concernant les investissements dans les infrastructures, la législation et bien d’autres domaines.
Un responsable souffle que la résilience hydrique et l’économie circulaire pourraient également être mentionnées.
Le commissaire à l’Agriculture, Christophe Hansen, a confié à POLITICO qu’il espérait que la question de l’adaptation au changement climatique serait abordée dans le discours de von der Leyen. “Nous devons faire davantage […] en matière d’atténuation du changement climatique, nous en sommes tous conscients, mais aussi en matière d’adaptation au changement climatique”, a-t-il déclaré.
Advertisement
Commerce
L’une des grandes questions sur le discours de von der Leyen est de savoir si elle évoquera la Chine.
Dans son discours de 2023, elle avait fait une annonce retentissante en révélant que la Commission lançait une enquête antisubventions sur les véhicules électriques chinois. Cette décision avait provoqué des représailles de Pékin, qui avait ciblé en retour les exportations européennes, notamment de viande de porc et de brandy.
Ce ne sera pas le cas cette fois-ci, selon un responsable, et l’Allemande n’annoncera pas de nouvelle enquête. Pékin ne tiendra pas une place très importante dans le discours, même si la présidente devrait insister sur la nécessité pour l’UE d’accélérer ses efforts de diversification et pourrait aller jusqu’à mentionner explicitement l’outil de diversification envisagé par la Commission.
Immigration
Le discours de von der Leyen intervient après la crise de Ceuta, au cours de laquelle des dizaines de milliers de migrants ont pénétré sur le territoire espagnol, provoquant des remous politiques au sein de l’Union européenne tout au long de l’été.
Le commissaire chargé de la Migration, Magnus Brunner, a présenté à ses collègues un rapport sur les enseignements tirés de cette affaire lors du séminaire de rentrée. Il a été le seul commissaire à faire une telle présentation, relate un responsable européen à POLITICO.
Ursula von der Leyen devrait profiter de son discours pour appeler au renforcement de Frontex, l’agence européenne chargée de la gestion des frontières. Cela implique notamment de multiplier par plus de trois le nombre de gardes-frontières et de garde-côtes européens, pour le porter à 30 000, contre environ 7 800 aujourd’hui, et d’étendre éventuellement le mandat et les pouvoirs de Frontex, selon trois responsables européens, afin de permettre à l’agence de jouer un rôle dans les “hubs de retour” situés dans des pays tiers.
Advertisement
Deux responsables ajoutent que l’Allemande pourrait ouvrir la voie à un financement des infrastructures frontalières (traduction : des clôtures) à l’aide de fonds européens — ce qui constituerait un changement significatif dans la position de la Commission. L’un d’eux indique aussi qu’elle pourrait suggérer d’utiliser les fonds européens pour aider les Etats membres à financer des hubs de retour en dehors de l’UE.
Mais, selon un diplomate de haut rang et un responsable de l’Union, l’idée la plus controversée envisagée pour ce discours est celle d’un cadre européen applicable aux situations de pression migratoire massive, qui permettrait de suspendre certaines règles en matière d’asile et d’accélérer les retours. Le Premier ministre grec Kyriakos Mitsotakis a lancé une idée similaire dans une récente tribune publiée par POLITICO.
Défense
La défense et la sécurité devraient également occuper une place importante dans ce discours, la stratégie de sécurité tant attendue étant prévue pour début octobre.
Un panneau signalant des travaux routiers est fixé à un panneau indiquant la frontière belge à Adinkerke, en Belgique, le 10 mai 2016. | Christopher Furlong/Getty Images
A l’origine, cette stratégie devait être présentée à l’issue du sommet de l’Otan à Ankara en juillet, et son report alimente les spéculations selon lesquelles Ursula von der Leyen profiterait de son discours pour prendre les devants sur ce document, en donnant un aperçu de certaines de ses idées et priorités clés.
La Commission prépare également une mise à jour de sa politique arctique, dont la publication est actuellement prévue le 20 octobre, et qui a été rebaptisée “stratégie pour le voisinage nordique et l’Arctique”, afin de refléter son champ géographique élargi. De retour d’un voyage au Groenland, Ursula von der Leyen a déclaré récemment que l’Europe souhaitait “s’engager davantage dans l’Arctique”.
Avec la venue du Premier ministre canadien Mark Carney cette semaine, l’Allemande pourrait annoncer une initiative en matière de sécurité dans l’Arctique en collaboration avec Ottawa, complète un responsable de l’UE. “La sécurité et la défense, c’est toujours son domaine de prédilection”, commente le même — en Allemagne, von der Leyen a été ministre de la Défense.
Advertisement
Un autre haut responsable souligne que von der Leyen recevait Mark Carney, et qu’un “bon hôte” offre des cadeaux, même s’il n’a pas pu préciser en quoi consisteraient ces cadeaux politiques.
Réseaux sociaux
Ursula von der Leyen a confirmé qu’elle profiterait de son discours pour dévoiler ses projets concernant les restrictions d’âge sur les réseaux sociaux, une proposition législative pouvant être présentée le jour même. Elle devra répondre à de nombreuses questions épineuses, notamment quel sera l’âge minimum fixé et si elle laissera les pays de l’UE définir leur propre limite d’âge.
La semaine dernière, lors d’un dîner ministériel à Dublin, les gouvernements nationaux n’ont pas réussi à s’entendre sur un chiffre, ont relaté trois responsables à POLITICO.
La Commission devrait également étendre les restrictions d’âge à d’autres services, tels que les plateformes de jeux vidéo et les chatbots IA.
“Nous ne sommes pas obligés d’accepter que l’enfance soit façonnée par des algorithmes”, a déclaré Ursula von der Leyen jeudi.

Türkiye’s 1st homegrown lunar spacecraft to be tested ahead of 2027 mission
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:33:37 UTC
01:33:37 KST

Zeynep Duyar, Mehmet Can Toptas and Emir Yildirim
14 September 2026•Update: 14 September 2026
Türkiye completed the production and assembly of its first lunar spacecraft, transferring the 3.5-metric-ton craft to Turkish Aerospace Industries (TAI) for environmental testing, the industry and technology minister said in a recent statement.
Mehmet Fatih Kacir said the craft is scheduled for launch from the Kennedy Space Center in early 2027 and will take around two months to reach a 100-kilometer (62.13-mile) polar orbit around the Moon.
The craft will operate in lunar orbit for three months, with the potential to extend its operation to a year and a half, during which solar winds, water formation, magnetic fields and surface radiation will be evaluated through homegrown scientific instruments.
Kacir stated that these efforts have been made to realize “a fully independent Türkiye in critical technologies,” following the country’s similar approach in its defense industry.
The spacecraft includes critical flight, communications and power systems developed for the previous Imece and Turksat 6A satellite projects, boasting an 80% domestic production rate.
“The further tests will verify the spacecraft’s ability to withstand the harsh conditions it will encounter during launch and in the space environment,” he said. The craft will then be transferred to a new cleanroom facility of the Turkish Scientific and Technological Research Institution (Tubitak) Space for final inspections.
The craft will use a homegrown hybrid propulsion system for orbit-raising maneuvers and a final controlled deceleration burn to reach the lunar surface at the end of the primary scientific mission.
“Only eight countries have carried out lunar missions so far, and when we implement our program, Türkiye will become the ninth country,” the minister noted.
These developments follow the country’s recent accession to the Artemis Accords, signed to promote global cooperation in the peaceful exploration of the Moon and deep space.
Kacir stated that development of the Turksat 7A communications satellite has begun alongside the design phases of the Imece-2 and Imece-3 Earth observation satellite constellations.
Meanwhile, Ankara is constructing a spaceport in Somalia to eventually provide independent access to space and reduce reliance on foreign launch facilities.
The Turkish government is also collaborating with the Turkish Space Agency and the Middle East Technical University (METU) to establish a space tech development zone in Ankara to extend the rapid growth of Turkish defense into the country’s space sector by integrating more tech startups with the national space manufacturing ecosystem.
The southwestern coastal city of Antalya will host the 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC 2026) from Oct. 5-9 to showcase these expanding capabilities to nearly 10,000 global participants.

British man accused of drugging and raping wife over two decades admits 60 offences
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:32:23 UTC
01:32:23 KST

A man has pleaded guilty to drugging and sexually assaulting his wife over a period of 20 years as he admitted 60 criminal offences.
The man, who cannot be named in order to protect the anonymity of his victim, is in his 60s and before his arrest lived in Stockport, Greater Manchester.
He admitted 60 counts, which include 21 counts of rape and sharing intimate images of his victim.
His estranged wife sat on the front row of the packed courtroom with other family members as he entered his pleas, occasionally sobbing as he did so.
In June, the man pleaded guilty to 15 of the charges against him. On Monday he admitted the final 45 at Manchester’s Minshull Street crown court.
The defendant also previously pleaded guilty to sharing intimate photographs or film of his wife, without her consent, for sexual gratification.
Twelve co-defendants all deny various allegations involving the same woman.
Rick Jackson, an assistant chief constable of Greater Manchester police, said: “Our focus remains on supporting the victim of this horrific campaign of abuse through what is a very complex investigation.
“Specialist support continues to be provided to the victim at the centre of this case.
“If you are concerned you, or someone you know, may be affected by drug-facilitated sexual abuse, please know that you do not need proof, certainty, or a clear memory to be taken seriously.
“You are not expected to understand exactly what has happened or who was involved in order to be taken seriously. If you feel that something has happened, then please report it or ask for help.”

By Day, He Taught Salsa in Russia. By Night, He Recruited Saboteurs Across Europe
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:31:29 UTC
01:31:29 KST

- Category
- World
By Day, He Taught Salsa in Russia. By Night, He Recruited Saboteurs Across Europe
A Cuban national living in Russia recruited a network of operatives to carry out sabotage and arson attacks across at least four European Union countries in 2024, according to a joint investigation by Deutsche Welle and three other European broadcasters.
The investigation identified the alleged recruiter as Oemis Romagoza Durruthy, a Cuban-born dance instructor based in Petrozavodsk in northern Russia who operated online under aliases including “Dios” and “Adrian.”
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to DW, accounts linked to Dios published recruitment advertisements on Telegram in 2024, targeting people seeking work in Poland, Cubans living in Russia, and Latin Americans with military backgrounds. Some advertisements sought candidates with experience in surveillance, reconnaissance, logistics, and tactical maneuvering, offering $1,500 as well as bonuses for completed operations.
After months of reporting, interviews with intelligence officials and people close to suspects, and analysis of confidential court records, official statements, social media posts, and leaked data, DW and its partners concluded that Dios recruited people to conduct sabotage operations benefiting Russia in at least four EU countries. Most of those recruited came from Spanish-speaking countries.
Among them was Luis Alfonso Murillo Diosa, a Colombian national and former soldier who initially sought to join the Ukrainian military in early 2024. Murillo joined a Facebook group for Latin Americans interested in fighting in Ukraine, where he was contacted by Dios.
According to confidential court documents reviewed by DW, Dios introduced himself as a member of a special group and instead offered Murillo “special tasks” in Europe. After Murillo accepted, Dios arranged his flights, accommodation, and ground transportation remotely, with the two never meeting in person.
When Murillo arrived in Bucharest in July 2024, Dios sent him a satellite image marking a waste-processing facility and an oil well. According to the investigation, Murillo was instructed to photograph and film the sites before setting them on fire.
Romanian authorities detained him near the waste-processing facility after he had taken photographs but before any arson took place. Murillo told investigators that he had not intended to start a fire, saying he had been trying to reach Europe before traveling to Ukraine and did not know who he was working for. In 2025, a Romanian court sentenced him to six years in prison for attempted sabotage.
DW and its partners established that Murillo was one of at least a dozen people recruited by Dios for sabotage operations across Europe. Such recruits are often described as “disposable agents,” people hired online who may have little or no knowledge of the identity of their handlers or the broader purpose behind their assignments.
The investigation found that over a four-month period in 2024, Dios instructed recruits to set fire to building-material warehouses in Poland, a bus depot in Czechia, a waste-processing facility in Romania, and Lithuanian-made equipment intended for Ukraine.
Lithuanian prosecutors were the only authorities cited in the investigation to have publicly linked this particular series of arson plots to Russian military intelligence. Lithuanian law enforcement also issued an international wanted notice for a Cuban national living in Russia.
By examining confidential court documents and dozens of leaked files, DW and its partners identified that individual as Oemis Romagoza Durruthy.
Originally from Camagüey, Cuba, Romagoza has lived in Russia for at least seven years and teaches Latin American dance in Petrozavodsk. He is listed as a contact for the local Made in Cuba dance studio, with videos online showing him teaching salsa, bachata, and kizomba.
Romagoza married a Russian woman in 2022 and later obtained Russian citizenship, according to the investigation. DW said it could not determine when or under what circumstances he allegedly began working for Russian intelligence services.
The investigation found indications that Romagoza may have experienced financial difficulties before the alleged recruitment operation began. Leaked records showed that he took out loans from several lenders in 2023. Several months later, he joined Facebook groups used by Latin Americans looking for work in Poland or seeking to fight for Ukraine, around the same period that Dios began publishing recruitment advertisements on Telegram.
The investigation placed the network within a broader pattern of suspected Russian sabotage operations in Europe following Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Conflict expert Keir Giles told DW that Russia increasingly turned to disposable agents after European governments expelled numerous Russian diplomats suspected of espionage and disinformation activities following the start of the invasion in 2022.
At least nine people recruited by Romagoza have been detained, according to DW. Two are already serving prison sentences of between six and eight years for attempted sabotage or terrorism, while the others are awaiting trial.
It remains unclear whether Romagoza continued recruiting operatives or organizing attacks after September 2024. However, DW reported that suspected Russian sabotage activities across Europe have continued, with authorities in several EU countries investigating more recent attacks and fires for possible links to Russia.
The investigation comes as European countries step up efforts to counter Russian hybrid operations. Germany and Ukraine recently agreed to deepen security cooperation against such threats, with Ukrainian intelligence and law enforcement specialists set to share their experience in countering drones, sabotage, espionage, and cyberattacks.

France Moves to Begin Rafale Training for Ukrainian Pilots Ahead of First Jet Deliveries

France Moves to Begin Rafale Training for Ukrainian Pilots Ahead of First Jet Deliveries
France is preparing to begin initial training for Ukrainian pilots who are expected to transition to Rafale fighter jets, as Kyiv moves toward adding the French-made aircraft to its combat aviation fleet.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to Le Figaro on September 13, France plans to launch the first stage of training for Ukrainian aircrews as part of preparations for the future operation of Rafale fighters.
France has several aircraft available for the early stages of the training pipeline, including GROB G 120TP trainers and Dornier Alpha Jet advanced training aircraft. These platforms allow pilots to develop skills in aircraft handling, navigation, and elements of air combat before moving to frontline fighter aircraft.
Training for Ukrainian pilots and maintenance personnel on the Rafale is expected to begin in France in 2026. The program would prepare both aircrews and ground personnel to operate and support the aircraft.
The first four Rafale fighters are expected to be transferred to the Ukrainian Air Force after the initial training program is completed. Plans also call for Ukraine to acquire an initial batch of 16 Rafale fighters together with the weapons and equipment required for their operation.
The first aircraft are expected to arrive in Ukraine in 2028–2029.
The program forms part of a broader effort to expand Ukraine’s Western-built fighter fleet. In November 2025, plans were reported for the potential acquisition of as many as 100 French Rafale fighters to strengthen Ukraine’s Air Force over the longer term.

Pope Leo XIV inaugurated AQVA – Catastrophe and Wonder on Monday, 14 September. Visitors enter through Diluvium, a 70-metre-long installation by French street artist JR, the first site-specific work commissioned for the exterior of the 16th-century library.
Inside, art and rare books explore water as both a source of life and a force of destruction. 3 Italian passengers fly out of Delhi without immigration clearance: What exactly happened
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:29:39 UTC
01:29:39 KST

3 Italian passengers flew from Amritsar to Munich without immigration clearance
NEW DELHI: The civil aviation ministry has issued a show-cause notice to Air India over alleged procedural lapses that allowed three Italian passengers to board a connecting flight from Delhi without completing immigration formalities earlier this month.The notice has been issued to the Air India CEO.The home ministry has also convened a meeting of stakeholders on Tuesday to discuss the incident, sources told news agency PTI.The three passengers flew from Amritsar to Delhi on September 4 before boarding a Lufthansa flight to Munich from Delhi airport. However, they did not complete the required immigration formalities at the airport, sources added.Titled “violation of SOP for hub and spoke operations resulting in three foreign nationals departing India without mandatory immigration clearance,” the show-cause notice issued to Air India last Saturday said the three passengers arrived in Delhi from Amritsar on AI 1115 at 12.50 am on September 4 and subsequently departed for Munich on a codeshare Lufthansa flight at 1.45 am, within an hour of their arrival.Home secretary Govind Mohan will chair a meeting on Tuesday to discuss the incident.The secretary and additional secretary of the civil aviation ministry, Intelligence Bureau director, additional secretary (UT and Foreigners) of the home ministry, Bureau of Immigration commissioner, Air India CEO and Delhi airport CEO are expected to attend the meeting, they added.
What exactly happened?
Amritsar airport is among the airports where Air India operates flights under its ‘Hub-and-Spoke’ model.
Under this arrangement, passengers complete immigration formalities at the airport of origin and can then travel to an overseas destination through a designated hub. At the hub airport, where the international flight departs, passengers are required only to undergo security checks before boarding.
For a passenger travelling from Amritsar via Delhi to an international destination, Amritsar serves as the spoke and Delhi as the hub.In the case of the three Italian passengers, sources said they were issued boarding passes at Amritsar for both their flight to Delhi and the Lufthansa flight to Munich.However, as the two flights were not covered under Air India’s ‘Hub-and-Spoke’ model, the passengers were required to exit through the arrival area at Delhi and complete immigration formalities before taking the Lufthansa flight.After arriving at Delhi airport, they were instead taken to the international transfer area and did not reach the immigration counter. They then boarded the flight to Munich without completing the immigration process, the sources said, as cited by PTI.Air India and Lufthansa have an interline partnership. An interline agreement generally allows passengers to book connecting flights operated by different airlines under a single itinerary.

MOSCOW, September 14. /TASS/. The BRICS summit held in New Delhi demonstrated the group's potential and made the West nervous about the irreversible collapse of the unipolar world order, Leonid Slutsky, Chairman of the State Duma Committee on International Affairs and leader of the LDPR party, told TASS while commenting on the summit's outcomes.

Ukraine to receive $841 million from World Bank amid budget deficit
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:28:57 UTC
01:28:57 KST

Ukraine will receive $841 million in budget support from the World Bank, backed by Canada's guarantees, in the near future, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi announced on Sep. 14.
The news comes as Ukraine faces its toughest budget situation since the start of Russia’s full-scale war in 2022, with Koretskyi previously saying the government was imposing strict limits on non-defense spending.
The funding will be provided under the Public Expenditures of Administrative Capacity Endurance (PEACE) in Ukraine, designed to support Ukraine's social and humanitarian expenditures. It will be used to reimburse pension payments from the state budget.
"Amid budget deficit and fiscal imbalance, this is rather crucial and timely support," Koretskyi wrote on social media.
Ukraine's Cabinet is due to submit a draft budget to parliament by Sep. 15 for revision and amendments.
The PEACE project in Ukraine was established in June 2022. In four years, it has mobilized a total of $53.5 billion to provide Kyiv with budgetary support during Russia's full-scale war, disclosed the Ukrainian government.
Canada is currently discussing the possibility of joining the EU's 90 billion-euro ($105 billion) support loan to Ukraine, the Financial Times (FT) reported on Sep.13. According to FT's sources familiar with the matter, Canada wants to finalize the size of its contribution by the EU-Canada Summit in October.

Passenger’s ‘bomb’ joke sparks chaos on Beirut-Paris flight
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:28:43 UTC

Breadcrumb
Passenger’s ‘bomb’ joke sparks chaos on Beirut-Paris flight
A passenger was detained in Lebanon after claiming he was carrying a bomb on a Middle East Airlines flight from Beirut to Paris on Monday, triggering a security alert and the evacuation and search of the aircraft before he later said he had been joking.
The MEA flight, numbered ME 229, was due to depart Beirut's Rafic Hariri International Airport for Paris at around 1pm.
Sources at Middle East Airlines told The New Arab that about 30 minutes before departure, the passenger claimed he was carrying a bomb while placing his bag in the overhead compartment.
The incident was immediately treated as a security threat, with all passengers ordered off the aircraft while security forces searched the plane and inspected passengers' luggage and belongings.
The passenger was detained for questioning and later told authorities that he had made the claim as a joke.
"The situation could only be handled in the way it was," an MEA source said.
"Anything of this nature must be treated as a security threat and cannot be dismissed as a joke. The lives of passengers and aviation safety are a priority, and all procedures must therefore be followed in accordance with security protocols."
The source apologised for the disruption caused by the incident, saying the passenger's actions had created confusion among travellers and delayed the flight.
Security sources separately told The New Arab that the passenger remained in custody while investigations continued and that the necessary legal measures would be taken against him.
According to his initial statement, the passenger said he had made the comment as a joke, which security sources described as a "heavy-handed joke".
The incident comes as Beirut airport undergoes a series of measures aimed at improving its operational efficiency, passenger experience and facilities, alongside heightened security procedures.
The airport has seen upgrades to its sanitary facilities and check-in counters, as well as improvements to the arrivals hall and tourism-related services. Work is also under way to introduce a "fast track" service aimed at streamlining passenger movement and speeding up procedures.
The measures form part of an ongoing effort to improve the airport's operational readiness, service quality and infrastructure in line with modern standards.
Last week, Prime Minister Nawaf Salam chaired a meeting to follow up on cabinet decisions concerning health, environmental safety and aviation safety measures around the airport.
Under the cabinet decisions, authorities agreed to begin implementing measures including a ban on keeping or raising birds of all types within five kilometres of the boundaries of Rafic Hariri International Airport.
Authorities will also take action against farms and slaughterhouses operating without legal licences, exceeding the limits of their licences or failing to comply with legally required conditions and standards.

The festival: “one of the iconic moments of Italian spirit and culture in the country”
14 September 2026, 18:29
ANSA English Desk

Link copiato

The Italian Ambassador to Ecuador, Giovanni Davoli, inaugurated the 2026 edition of the “Passione Italia” Festival on Saturday, September 12, in Quito. According to a press release, this is the eighth edition of an initiative organized by the Italian Chamber of Commerce in Ecuador (CCIE), which drew nearly 2,000 paying attendees eager to spend a family day immersed in Italian culture.

Satellite images show 21 shelters at suspected Russian naval drone base at Lake Donuzlav in occupied Crimea
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:28:06 UTC
01:28:06 KST

At least 21 protected shelters have been built on the shore of Lake Donuzlav in Russian-occupied Crimea. They are likely intended to protect Russian naval drones.
The suspected base was first identified by the Ukrainian open-source intelligence (OSINT) project CyberBoroshno, and naval researcher H. I. Sutton later analyzed satellite imagery of the site. Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty’s project Krym.Realii highlighted their findings in a report on Sept. 4.
CyberBoroshno first reported the existence of the structures near Novoozerne on Sept. 1. The project’s analysts said the hangars were likely intended to store unmanned surface vessels (USVs) — remotely operated or autonomous boats.
The analysts said Russian forces have not yet been seen using these drones extensively in combat, but the construction of specialized infrastructure may indicate preparations for their future deployment. Using CyberBoroshno’s findings, H. I. Sutton examined satellite imagery of Donuzlav and counted at least 21 shelters at two sites along the lake’s southern shore.
According to his analysis, construction of the first eight shelters began in February 2026, while another eight appeared soon afterward. The second site was later expanded to 13 shelters. Roads are seen leading up to the shelters, allowing boats and equipment to be transported to the water. The shelters could be used to store, prepare, and launch the drones.
On Sept. 2, one day after CyberBoroshno published its findings, the Ukrainian Navy reported that it had destroyed a Russian Kama unmanned surface vessel near Snake Island. It is not currently known where the craft was launched from.
Russia officially unveiled the Kama for the first time in June 2026. According to its stated specifications, the vessel can operate up to 700 kilometers from its base and carry a payload of up to 600 kilograms.
Russia has already used naval drones in its war against Ukraine, but so far only in limited numbers, according to a source interviewed by Krym.Realii who previously served in Ukrainian military intelligence. The source said most of the military unmanned boats Russia has publicly displayed remain at the testing or prototype stage, with no evidence that they are being produced at scale.
In July, Russian Navy commander-in-chief Alexander Moiseyev announced the country was building its first 500-metric-ton unmanned vessel for hunting submarines and other underwater targets. The announcement drew criticism from several pro-war Russian Telegram channels and commentators, who argued that the Russian Navy should first establish mass production of small, inexpensive attack drones of the kind Ukraine has used extensively against Russian ships and infrastructure.

Portugal's foreign minister warned Monday that Israel's expanding illegal settlements and mounting economic pressure in the occupied West Bank and East Jerusalem were eroding prospects for the establishment of a viable Palestinian state.
Foreign Minister Paulo Rangel said Israel's E1 settlement plan was "extremely pernicious" because it would divide the West Bank, isolate East Jerusalem and was incompatible with a two-state solution.
Israel's withholding of Palestinian tax revenues amounted to a "brutal strangulation" of the Palestinian Authority's finances, preventing the economy from functioning, he said after meeting Palestinian Foreign Minister Varsen Aghabekian Shahin in Lisbon.
Rangel also cited the closure of Christian schools in East Jerusalem as evidence of worsening conditions there.
Portugal recognized the State of Palestine a year ago.
Rangel said the two-state solution was the only way to guarantee peaceful coexistence between Israelis and Palestinians.
Israel said last week it was closing Britain's consulate in East Jerusalem in response to plans by the U.K., France and Canada to block imports from illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank.

Microsoft sets provisional AI guidelines as industry leaders weigh safety slowdown
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:25:01 UTC
01:25:01 KST

Sumeyye Eryilmaz
14 September 2026•Update: 14 September 2026
- Framework prioritizes maintaining human control over automated capabilities
US technology corporation Microsoft unveiled a draft governance framework on Monday to regulate its artificial intelligence systems, establishing safety parameters aimed at ensuring future models remain strictly under human supervision.
The draft rules, titled the Humanist AI Code of Conduct, establish core operating boundaries and values for future systems developed by the company.
The framework prioritizes maintaining human control over automated capabilities.
Under the document, the software provider explicitly rejects the pursuit of all-purpose superintelligence that might evade oversight mechanisms, maintaining that systems must be designed to halt operations rather than breach conduct constraints.
It also explicitly stipulates that models will never resist human interruption, override, correction, or shutdown, and must always comply with a request to pause, redirect, cancel, or stop operations.
The publication opens a six-week public consultation window to gather external perspectives from ethicists, researchers, policymakers, and the public.
Following revisions toward the end of the year, Microsoft plans to implement the policy to guide model development in 2027 and beyond.
"We got feedback from people that they wanted to see even more explicit commitment to AI always working in service of people and not trying to replace them," Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman told television broadcaster CNBC.
Advanced artificial intelligence systems must remain firmly under human oversight while developers pursue deliberate pacing to ensure safe deployment, Microsoft Chairman and CEO Satya Nadella said Sunday.
The guidelines arrive days after executives from rival AI firms OpenAI and Anthropic agreed to slow the pace of development amid safety concerns.

URCS pays over UAH 110 mln to residents of frontline communities over two-month period
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
19:23:10 EEST
01:23:10 KST

Over the past two months, the Ukrainian Red Cross Society (URCS) has disbursed more than UAH 110 million to residents of frontline regions.
"In July and August, the Ukrainian Red Cross distributed more than UAH 110 million in financial aid to residents of frontline regions… 9,759 people received financial aid," the society said on Facebook on Monday.
Financial assistance is being distributed on a priority basis in Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhia, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Sumy, Kharkiv, Kherson, and Chernihiv regions.
Financial assistance is provided to people who have been affected by shelling, were forced to evacuate, or belong to vulnerable population groups living in frontline communities and are unable to meet their basic needs. The funds received help people independently identify their most urgent needs – such as buying food and medicine, paying for housing and utilities, relocating to a new place, restoring their daily lives, and covering other necessary daily expenses.
The Ukrainian Red Cross Society is implementing the program with support from the U.S. government, the Norwegian Red Cross, the Danish Red Cross, and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.

French-Slovak veto deepens EU deadlock on Russia sanctions renewal
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:21:25 UTC
01:21:25 KST

Paris seeks to remove Usmanov from the sanctions list in an apparent quid-pro-quo move to secure the release of detained French nationals.
France is pressing for Russian-Uzbek businessman Alisher Usmanov to be removed from the EU sanctions list in an effort to secure the release of an unspecified number of French nationals detained in Azerbaijan, according to several officials and diplomats familiar with the negotiations.
The French position has complicated efforts in Brussels to renew EU sanctions on Russia, which cover almost 3,000 individuals and entities accused of supporting Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The measures are due to expire this month.
The deadlock was initially driven by Slovakia, which has long called for Usmanov to be removed from the sanctions list, for separate reasons.
France joined Bratislava in calling for his delisting on Friday to the surprise of diplomats, Euronews reported.
EU ambassadors agreed on Monday to extend the sanctions for one week, until 22 September, giving member states more time to reach an agreement. If no agreement is reached, all Russian nationals will be delisted, adding to the sense of urgency.
"France isn't for budging, but it would send the absolute wrong message at the wrong time," one official said, speaking on condition of anonymity.
"I'm not sure what will change in a week."
Most member states remain opposed to removing names from the sanctions list while Russia continues its war in Ukraine and amid concerns over hybrid attacks in Europe.
However, some officials acknowledge that France has cited national security concerns, a principle applied to critical issues. The French government declined to comment.
"Everything has an explanation," one diplomat said.
Still, the last-minute move has frustrated diplomats who oppose removing any Russian nationals from the sanctions list.
One diplomat familiar with the talks said Paris' quid-pro-quo approach effectively amounted to a veto of a common EU position, reminiscent of tactics employed by Hungary under Viktor Orbán.
France, meanwhile, insists it remains one of the bloc's strongest supporters of sanctions against Russia.
The Financial Times first reported about the prisoner swap in Azerbaijan.
Usmanov was added to the EU sanctions list in the early days of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The EU Council cited his "close ties" with Russian President Vladimir Putin and his interests in "key sectors" of the Russian economy.
Usmanov denies the allegations and has vigorously pushed to be removed from the list.
Slovakia has also long called for Usmanov and fellow Russian businessman Mikhail Fridman to be removed from the sanctions list. Other EU member states have so far rejected the request, which they regard as politically motivated.
Earlier this year, a media investigation published a two-page letter sent by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan to Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico, asking for assistance in ending what Erdoğan described as the "unfair practice" involving Usmanov.
"Your support in removing him from the EU sanctions list and restoring his violated rights would be extremely valuable," Erdoğan wrote in the letter, dated 2 March 2026.
The document said Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan also supported Usmanov's removal.
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy criticised the state of negotiations in his evening address on Monday, name checking Usmanov and Fridman.
"This is definitely not the time to lift sanctions, to rescue Russian oligarchs from them, and definitely not the time for Europe to give Russia gifts," Zelenskyy said.
"Usmanov, Fridman, and other Russian figures like them have not made their moves against the war so far. This is not the time for Europe to forget what is happening."

Israeli documentary NAZA exposes Gaza killing system, wins Venice jury prize
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:20:24 UTC
01:20:24 KST

ALBAWABA- An Israeli documentary exposing what its filmmakers describe as a systematic system for the killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza has won the Special Jury Prize at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival, placing Israeli war crimes and the treatment of Palestinian civilian deaths at the center of one of the world’s leading film events.
NAZA, directed by Israeli filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, is based on testimony from 24 Israeli military and intelligence insiders interviewed anonymously.
The film examines Israel’s bombing campaign in Gaza and the systems used to select targets and estimate expected civilian casualties, including the use of artificial-intelligence-assisted targeting. Its title refers to a military intelligence term used to indicate the number of civilians expected to be killed in an airstrike.
Shot secretly at night on rooftops in Tel Aviv, the 80-minute documentary was presented in the official competition on September 10. It received a reported 25-minute standing ovation, one of the most striking reactions of this year’s festival. The film was produced by The Guardian and JW Films, with Jonathan Glazer, director of The Zone of Interest, among its executive producers.
The filmmakers, who were also among the directors of the Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land, argue that the testimonies reveal not isolated battlefield mistakes but a broader system in which the killing of Palestinian civilians has been incorporated into military decision-making. The film builds partly on investigations previously published by The Guardian, +972 Magazine and Local Call.
Accepting the Venice award, Abraham said the Israeli military campaign had produced systemic mass killing and urged Israelis to watch the film and confront the consequences of their country's actions in Gaza.
The documentary has provoked a fierce political backlash in Israel. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned Israeli filmmakers for portraying the Israel Defense Forces as perpetrators of war crimes, saying that such accusations coming from inside Israel were unacceptable. Israel's military has rejected the allegations in the documentary, particularly questioning the use of anonymous testimonies.
The controversy escalated after Culture Minister Miki Zohar called for Abraham and Szor to have their Israeli citizenship revoked, accusing them of treason. The demand has intensified debate over freedom of expression in Israel and the treatment of domestic criticism of the Gaza war.
The significance of NAZA extends beyond cinema. At a time when Gaza's devastation and Israeli violations of international law remain under intense international scrutiny, the documentary offers an account from within Israel's own military and intelligence establishment.
Its success at Venice, and the backlash it triggered at home, has renewed attention to questions of civilian targeting, military accountability and the alleged systematic nature of Israel’s conduct in Gaza. According to Gaza’s Health Ministry and human rights organizations, Israel has killed more than 80,000 Palestinians since October 7, including more than 23,000 children, making the war one of the deadliest conflicts to have devastated the besieged enclave.

After losing son, couple welcomes daughter born from embryo frozen for 22 years
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:17:53 UTC
01:17:53 KST

Months after son killed in crash, couple welcomes daughter born from embryo frozen for 22 years
Out of their darkest moment, a Greek couple managed to make a new start with a baby born last week. Doing so meant using one of Cristina Rapti‑Tzelepi's decades-old embryos and racing to beat a government deadline.
Just months after their 21‑year‑old son died in a road crash in October, Rapti‑Tzelepi, now 54, and her husband made the decision to pursue another attempt using an embryo frozen for 22 years.
Rapti-Tzelepi was running up against the Greek government's 54-year age limit for women to complete in vitro fertilization procedures and secure approval from a national authority. When she started, time was already running short.
"I only had a 2½-month window," she told The Associated Press. "It was stressful, but with inner strength and our doctor and his whole team by our side, we got through every obstacle."
She gave birth on Wednesday in the Greek capital, Athens, to a girl who weighed in at 7 pounds, 11 ounces. In a hospital room brightened with pink balloons and flowers on Friday, the new parents were overcome with emotion.
"We decided to give life a second chance, to make a new start, bring new life into our home and keep our family's story going," Rapti-Tzelepi said, sitting on her bed in black pajamas. "My wish for her is to grow up healthy and happy, full of joy like our first child, who filled our home with laughter."
The child was born using the woman's embryo that had been frozen more than 22 years ago, an unusually long time for a frozen fertilized egg to be used to produce a pregnancy.
Last year, an Ohio couple welcomed a baby boy developed from an embryo frozen for more than 30 years through a process known as "embryo adoption," and earned recognition from Guinness World Records as the oldest human embryo used in a successful pregnancy.
Dr. Kostas Pantos, Rapti-Tzelepi's gynecologist and head of the Hellenic Society of Reproductive Medicine, argued that Greece's age restrictions warrant review, noting the country's steep birth rate decline.
"The law is very strict: 54 plus one day is not allowed. Maybe it's time for it to change," said Pantos, a native of Melbourne, Australia. "I think it's a right (parents) should not be deprived of."
The baby's 60-year-old father, Constantinos Raptis, held his new daughter as she slept on his shoulder, wrapped in a white bodysuit. He said that he was deeply grateful to the doctor for restoring hope to his family.
"He took us by the hand and pulled us out of our deepest darkness," Raptis said. "We escaped from that darkness, and I believe we have a lot to live for now."
The couple named their daughter Georgia in honor of their late son, Giorgos, also born thanks to IVF. They haven't ruled out trying for another child — possibly by traveling abroad.
As CBS News reported in November, embryo donation is gaining in popularity in the U.S. Frozen donated embryo transfers in the United States nearly quadrupled from 2004 to 2019, according to a study published in the American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology. It's estimated there are currently more than 1 million frozen embryos in the U.S. — many from those reluctant to discard them after they are done with their cycles of IVF.

Modern war that the US is not ready for: For the price of one American cruise missile, Russia builds 20 “poor-man” drones and missiles
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
16:17:48 UTC
01:17:48 KST

Russia has fielded a new generation of cheap, jet-powered drones and cruise missiles faster than Ukraine or the US can build defenses against them, according to The Wall Street Journal. The weapons run on Chinese parts that slip past Western sanctions, and they are already getting through air defenses designed to stop slower drones. Analysts say the West underestimated how fast Moscow could move from an idea to a full assembly line.
Russia now leans on cheap, mass-produced drones to swamp Ukraine's air defenses with sheer numbers night after night, and its factories keep growing to keep the attacks coming. The bigger lesson reaches past this war: in a long fight, cheap weapons in large numbers can beat a small stock of expensive ones.
A cheap weapon that gets past Ukraine's defenses
Ukraine had learned to shoot down the Iran-designed Shahed drones Russia was launching. Then Moscow moved the goalposts. The newest model, the Geran-5, looks more like a missile than a drone—Mike Monnik, head of the drone-threat firm DroneSec, called it "essentially a poor-man's cruise missile," and it forced a rewrite of Ukraine's counter-drone playbook. The Geran-5 and the Banderol cruise missiles are each estimated to cost about $100,000. A US Tomahawk costs more than $2 million.
Russia built five more halls for the drones it assembles using Chinese parts to hit Ukrainian cities
Built fast, with China's help
Moscow needed only about two years to take each weapon from the drawing board to the battlefield, reworking earlier designs, testing them in combat, and pushing them into serial production. Ukrainian assessments, echoed by the drone-intelligence firm DroneSec, trace the leap to Chinese parts—the turbojet engines, the navigation computers, the radios—most of them off-the-shelf, dual-use gear anyone can buy. The weapons are aimed at Ukrainian cities and infrastructure—a Banderol struck a residential area of Kharkiv in July.
An expensive problem for the West
US forces and NATO have knocked down cheap drones with costly Patriot interceptors and fighter jets, often firing several interceptors at a single weapon. Western firms that built interceptors for slow drones are now scrambling to make faster, jet-powered ones. Kateryna Bondar of the Center for Strategic and International Studies said the West keeps underestimating how fast Russia turns experiments into production, and that Kyiv had years of warning yet was still caught off guard.
"I'm surprised everyone is surprised," she said.
At NATO's July summit in Ankara, members committed more than $40 billion to counter-drone defenses over the coming five years.
