Lockheed Plans to Fly ‘Vectis’ CCA by End of 2027, Already Working on More Aircraft
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
10:05:00 UTC
19:05:00 KST

Lockheed Martin’s proposed autonomous drone, called Vectis, is still on track to fly a prototype by the end of 2027, an official from the company’s Skunk Works division said Sept. 10, and the firm already started work on four more Vectis aircraft.
“The team is extremely excited as these parts start to come together [for Vectis], to actually get the wheels off the ramp by the end of 2027,” Ron Fehlen, vice president and general manager of Skunk Works, said in a conference call with reporters.
Lockheed first unveiled Vectis last September, ahead of AFA’s Air, Space & Cyber Conference, and officials said at the time they hoped to fly within two years.
This year, Fehlen told reporters Lockheed chose to begin work on the additional four Vectis aircraft “to lean into it,” and to have more aircraft to expand testing and further advance production efforts.
Vectis is a Group 5 drone, meaning it weighs more than 1,320 pounds and usually flies above 18,000 feet, the same category as the MQ-9A Reaper and the Air Force’s Collaborative Combat Aircraft, the FQ-42 and FQ-44. It will be roughly 34 feet long with a wingspan of 38 feet, Fehlen said, and images released by Lockheed show it has a lambda wing design, with no tail.
Vectis will have autonomous capabilities, using Lockheed’s MDCX autonomy command and control platform that has also controlled the Navy’s MQ-25 Stingray drone, and will be able to carry out multiple missions. Fehlen did not directly address questions about Vectis’ stealth capabilities, aside from saying it will be survivable. Fehlen also did not detail the drone’s loadout or weapons capabilities, but a video released by Lockheed showed Vectis would carry weapons in an internal bay.
As a potential CCA for the Air Force or another customer, Vectis could be controlled both from a ground station as well as teamed up with crewed fighters as a drone wingman, Fehlen said. The pilots flying alongside Vectis would direct it using a touchscreen interface like a tablet.
The Air Force is developing a fleet of at least 1,000 semi-autonomous CCA drones to expand its combat “mass” at a lower cost than fielding more manned fighters. The first iteration of CCAs, made by General Atomics Aeronautical Systems and Anduril Industries, will specialize in air-to-air capabilities, but more “increments” will follow. Air Force officials said Sept. 3 the service has a cost target of $20 million for CCA’s air vehicles, not counting additional systems such as sensors.
Fehlen said Lockheed envisions Vectis as appealing to multiple customers, including the U.S. Air Force and Navy and international customers. Lockheed declined to comment on the potential price tag for Vectis, aside from saying it will be offered at a competitive price point for CCAs.
Fehlen said Skunk Works is leveraging multiple advancements and technologies it developed for other programs—including work on complex air vehicles, advanced design and manufacturing processes, autonomy, and artificial intelligence—into Vectis.
Vectis was designed using fully digital processes, Fehlen said, which is “creating that unbroken digital thread, from the design all the way through sustainment.”
Development work on those additional four Vectis CCAs is now under way, Fehlen said, and is moving faster in part due to the digital design process.
“It is a survivable, autonomous multimission platform, which we believe is the solution needed within today’s operational environment and into the future,” Fehlen said. “So we’re making that strategic investment to accelerate the production progress and the maturity of Vectis. It’s an imperative that we do this to deliver the capability our nation and our allies desperately need.”
The Air Force and Lockheed’s experiments earlier this year with AI-controlled intercepts using the X-62 VISTA plane—a heavily modified test F-16D loaded with autonomous capabilities—have also helped shape Skunk Works’ approach to Vectis, Fehlen said. In those tests, the VISTA conducted 27 AI-controlled intercepts of a live T-38 Talon jet during eight sorties.
Fehlen highlighted the submerged inlet on Vectis’ dorsal side as a key design attribute, one which he said would reduce drag on the aircraft and help increase its flight range. And in situations where Vectis might have to take off from rough runways, like under the Air Force’s Agile Combat Employment concept, having the vent on top of the drone could help reduce chances of debris getting sucked into the inlet.
Vectis’ tail-less design will also help reduce drag and maximize range, Fehlen said.
Lockheed is also concentrating on keeping the building process for Vectis simple, to lower costs and speed up production. Part of that is by reducing the number of parts required to build it. The firm will build these CCAs using a process called minimal tooling determinate assembly, which Fehlen compared to the way ready-to-assemble furniture is sold with holes already drilled and aligned for consumers to put together easily. Using minimal tooling determinate assembly would dramatically reduce the amount of labor needed to build Vectis, Fehlen said, as well as cutting down on the number of times workers have to go back and redo steps in the process by getting it right the first time.

21 killed in multi-vehicle crash in South Africa
Unknown
Unknown Publisher

10:04:46 UTC
19:04:46 KST

Hassan Isilow
14 September 2026•Update: 14 September 2026
At least 21 people were killed and four others seriously injured in an accident involving multiple vehicles in South Africa’s Western Cape province, the Road Traffic Management Corporation (RTMC) said on Monday.
The agency said the crash took place on Sunday night at 11.30 pm local time (0930 GMT) on the N1 highway, involving two minibus vehicles and a station wagon.
The collision on N1 between the towns of Prince Albert and Leeu-Gamku led to the closure of the highway in both directions, with motorists urged to take alternative routes, expect delays and exercise extreme caution.
South Africans depend on minibus taxis as their main mode of transport. The 14-seat taxis transport millions of people to work, schools, provinces, towns, and even across the borders daily.

Cambodia files complaint over alleged Thai chemical weapons use
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
10:04:16 UTC
19:04:16 KST

Cambodia has filed a complaint with the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons over allegations that the Thai military used chemical weapons and chemical substances during last year's border conflict, Cambodian media reported.
The complaint was filed on September 11 following findings by the Cambodian Mine Action Centre, which said 395 Cambodian civilians and security personnel were affected by the alleged substances, according to the Phnom Penh Post.
Heng Ratana, director-general of the centre, said the substances were allegedly delivered by aircraft and drones as well as through 155mm and 120mm artillery shells.
Evidence was found in civilian areas, including a market, villages and farmland, he said.
“Chemical weapons and chemical substances were used. From a technical perspective, these are two different terms,” the Phnom Penh Post quoted Ratana as saying.
Thailand rejects the allegations
The centre also cited an analysis of 61 chemical samples from August 2025, classifying one finding as a chemical weapon under the Chemical Weapons Convention and 22 as toxic or hazardous chemicals not prohibited by the treaty.
The complete laboratory report and sampling methodology were not presented during the briefing.
Thailand has previously rejected Cambodian allegations that its forces used chemical weapons.
Thailand's foreign ministry in July 2025 called the allegations “groundless” and part of a campaign of disinformation.
The Royal Thai Army later also rejected claims involving white phosphorus munitions, saying they are not classified as chemical weapons under the Chemical Weapons Convention.

Power and diesel prices heading for nearly two-year high
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
10:04:11 UTC
19:04:11 KST

Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen of the Social Democrats said Monday that she is “quite optimistic” Denmark, Greenland and the USA can reach an agreement on security and defense in Greenland.
Frederiksen spoke at a news conference in Finland, where she attended a European summit focused on security in the Arctic.
“We have agreed to start a high-level working group on closer cooperation on security and defense, also in Greenland,” Frederiksen said.
“As long as the working group between Greenland, Denmark, and the USA continues its work, it is too early to draw a conclusion. But I am quite optimistic that we will succeed in finding a way,” she said.
Frederiksen visited Greenland last week with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.
Denmark is among 10 NATO countries conducting a joint military exercise in Greenland. The exercise is intended to show that Denmark and NATO are protecting Greenland and the Arctic.
US President Donald Trump has criticized Denmark for not doing enough to protect Greenland from threats posed by Russia and China.
During the first weeks of September, 400 soldiers from 10 NATO countries are operating on land, at sea and in the air near Narsarsuaq and Kangerlussuaq. They are training to operate in Arctic conditions as part of NATO’s Arctic Sentry surveillance and deterrence mission.
“If one is to be able to operate in the Arctic, one has to train up here,” Søren Andersen, head of Denmark’s Arctic Command, told the Danish news agency Ritzau last week.
Andersen said the temporary Arctic Shield exercise is part of a long-term strategy for Greenland and the Arctic.
“For us, it is about helping to transform NATO’s northern flank into a hard target. Meaning all the way from Alaska across Canada, Greenland, and to the northern part of Norway,” he said.
Denmark and Greenland are also discussing whether to give the USA greater access to Greenland. The New York Times reported in the spring, based on American sources, that the USA wants three bases in Greenland as part of a possible agreement. Narsarsuaq and Kangerlussuaq were reportedly among the possible locations.
Danish Defense Minister Jeppe Bruus of the Social Democrats declined to discuss the working group’s talks during a visit to Narsarsuaq last week.
“I cannot comment on that. What goes on in that working group, goes on in that working group,” Bruus told Ritzau.
Bruus said the government wants to extend the operating period of Narsarsuaq Airport by one year if it receives support from the Folketing, Denmark’s parliament.
“Initially, it is a one-year extension. That gives us the opportunity to extend the playing board,” Bruus said.
Chief of Defense Michael Hyldgaard said Narsarsuaq would be an obvious possible location for an American base because of its position in southern Greenland and its access to transatlantic routes, the Denmark Strait and the GIUK gap.
The GIUK gap is the sea area between Greenland, Iceland and the United Kingdom. It is an important military passage where NATO can monitor and block Russian submarines moving toward the Atlantic.
The USA previously operated a military base in Narsarsuaq from July 1941 to November 1958.

Belgian provincial govt fires Muslim teacher after she refuses to remove her headscarf despite ban
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
10:04:02 UTC
19:04:02 KST

The provincial government of East Flanders in Belgium dismissed a teacher who refused to comply with a ban on religious symbols in provincial schools, broadcaster VRT reported on Monday.
Hadija Amajoud, who has taught at a provincial special education school in Assenede since 2022, was wearing a headscarf when she began working at the school.
A disciplinary procedure was launched after Amajoud made clear that she did not intend to remove her headscarf while teaching.
The ACOD trade union said it intends to challenge the dismissal before the Chamber of Appeal in Brussels, saying that the case could establish an important precedent concerning religious freedom and neutrality in education.
Amajoud questioned how far an employer can go in restricting a teacher's personal freedom and described the provincial administration's interpretation of neutrality as "purely political."
"Actually, no one is neutral. Every teacher stands in front of a class with his or her own convictions," she said.
Discrimination, intimidation
The provincial administration defended the dismissal, arguing it was required to enforce personnel regulations approved through the democratic process.
A ban on religious and political symbols has been in force in all schools operated by the province since the beginning of the current school year.
Under the regulations, teachers and students are prohibited from wearing badges, symbols or clothing that express political or religious convictions.
Six students and several organisations later challenged the measure before Belgium's Council of State, but the court ruled against the challengers in May.
Rights organisations and advocacy groups have largely criticised recent bans in Belgium, framing them as discriminatory, particularly against Muslim women and girls.
The Flemish Institute for Human Rights had previously found discrimination and intimidation in Amajoud's case.
Earlier in March, the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) condemned the ban imposed in East Flanders, saying that the restriction on hijab was meant to “promote their bigoted agendas.”
CAIR National Communications Director Ibrahim Hooper said that people of all backgrounds should be allowed to “dress as they please based on the dictates of their conscience and the principles of their faith.”

Autumn week starts dry, turns to rain showers
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
10:04:00 UTC
19:04:00 KST

Denmark is set for a week of changing autumn weather, with periods of rain, sunshine and mild temperatures, according to the Danish Meteorological Institute, DMI.
Monday began cool, particularly in central Jutland, where temperatures fell to between 6 and 8 degrees.
“The temperature is down to 6-8 degrees, so if you are going out cycling, you can clearly feel that autumn has arrived,” DMI duty meteorologist Jesper Eriksen told Ritzau.
The rest of Monday is expected to remain dry, with a mix of sunshine and clouds. Temperatures will reach between 15 and 18 degrees, with light to moderate winds from the west.
### Tuesday to be warmest day
Tuesday is expected to be the warmest day of the week.
Winds will turn to the south, bringing slightly warmer air over Denmark and pushing temperatures to between 17 and 21 degrees.
There will be periods of sunshine, although some rain is possible, particularly in Jutland.
More rain is expected to reach Jutland later Tuesday afternoon before moving east during the evening and overnight.
Wednesday will bring some sunshine but also showers.
Temperatures are expected to fall back to between 15 and 18 degrees, while winds will turn west again.
Thursday and Friday are expected to bring periods of rain and showers, with temperatures remaining between 15 and 18 degrees.
Winds from the west and southwest are also expected to strengthen gradually toward the end of the week.
Eriksen said the week would not be particularly cold despite the unsettled weather.
“In the week as a whole, you will not need the really warm clothes, but in periods you will need rainwear and rubber boots,” he said.
It remains unclear whether September will bring another spell of warmer weather later in the month.
“We will have to see what happens, whether the last spasms with some warmth arrive. It is not decided yet,” Eriksen said.

CPH Half will expand to 45,000 runners for its race on September 19, 2027, because of high demand, organizer Sparta Atletik og Løb, a Danish athletics and running organization, said in a news release.
Around 35,000 people are taking part in this year’s half marathon, up from about 32,000 in 2025.
Tickets for the 2027 race will be sold through a lottery instead of on a first-come, first-served basis.
Registration for the lottery opens September 16 and remains open for two weeks. People can register alone or in groups of up to three. Each group will either be selected together or not selected at all.
Selected runners will have 48 hours to buy a ticket. The price is DKK 795 plus a small administration fee.
“When demand is so high, access to the bib numbers must also function in a way where everyone has a fair and equal chance of getting a bib number,” Dorte Vibjerg, CEO of Sparta Atletik og Løb, said in the release.
The organizers also used a lottery to sell tickets for this year’s CPH Half, which is part of the World Athletics Road Running Championships. Similar systems are used for major marathons in Berlin and London.
This year’s race starts Sunday. Elite international runners will begin first, followed by the other participants.
Danish police brought 79 new charges linked to possible crime-for-hire cases from January through the end of July, the Ministry of Justice said Monday.
In total, police brought 316 charges from April 2024 through the end of July this year that may involve crime-for-hire, a practice also known as “Violence as a Service.”
The figures come from NSK, a Danish police unit that handles serious and organized crime. In January, authorities had recorded 237 charges, according to figures released by the ministry in February.
The government disclosed the latest figures as it sent a bill proposing stricter penalties and other measures against gangs and crime-for-hire for consultation. That process allows judges, lawyers, police and other groups to submit concerns or objections before the proposal moves forward.
The bill would increase penalties for crime-for-hire and treat criminal families in the same way as gangs.
“We will not tolerate children and young people being recruited into a life of crime, and residential areas being marked by fear, control, and parallel power structures,” Justice Minister Nicolai Wammen of the Social Democrats said in a statement.
The proposal would also add a provision to the penal code intended to make it easier to convict people who provide minor services to gang leaders.
Other measures include allowing background checks for dockworkers and increasing the penalty for violating a stay ban. Police have recorded a large increase in such violations.
A stay ban can be imposed on a person who has committed a crime connected to a gang. It prevents that person from entering a specific area, such as part of a town or municipality, for a set period.
Violating a stay ban currently carries a fine of 10,000 DKK. Under the proposed law, a violation would result in 30 days in prison.
Power and diesel prices heading for nearly two-year high
The electricity price on Monday evening is the highest level in almost two years, when the price exceeds seven kroner per kilowatt-hour. The energy company OK writes this in a press release Monday morning.
According to Troels Skipper, commercial director at OK, the high electricity price is due to a combination of rising gas prices and a lack of wind and solar energy.
“Right now, we are in the unfortunate situation where the high gas price pushes the electricity price up along with it. And unfortunately, we do not get enough electricity production from wind turbines and solar cells to push the price the other way,” he said.
The last time the hourly price was at around seven DKK per kilowatt-hour was in December 2024.

More than half of the Danish schools that were selected for the latest Pisa survey declined to participate. In total, 398 schools were drawn for the survey. Of those, 215 chose not to participate, writes Kristeligt Dagblad.
When a selected school chooses to decline, a reserve school could step in. In advance, two reserve schools had been designated for each of the drawn schools.
Therefore, a total of 283 schools ended up participating in the survey. However, this is significantly fewer than in 2022, when 347 schools participated.
According to Kristeligt Dagblad, the number also remains below the OECD’s “technical minimum requirement”.
According to Monika Klingsbjerg-Besrechel, chief consultant at Statistics Denmark, which was responsible for the practical part of the survey, the many declines have not affected the quality of the survey.
“Fortunately, we reached a higher response rate, but despite that, we were unfortunately still below the minimum requirement from the OECD. If we had not had the reserve schools, we really would have been in serious trouble,” she says to Kristeligt Dagblad.
She points out that it was subsequently investigated whether the many declines had affected the result.

Danmarks Idrætsforbund (DIF) has announced Silkeborg as the first of five host cities for the 2027 edition of the Royal Run, making it the first time the Central Jutland city is on the bill for the event.
“I am wildly happy about the news that we will be a host city for Royal Run in 2027, and I am looking forward very much to welcoming a public celebration in running shoes right in the middle of Silkeborg,” said the city’s mayor, Helle Gade.
Thus, the run moves to the city that also brands itself under the name ‘Denmark’s Outdoor Capital’, something the mayor looks forward to showcasing.
“Here in Søhøjlandet we have a unique setting for both participants and spectators with hilly landscapes, great viewpoints over the Silkeborg lakes, and an exciting city center where urban life and nature merge. I look forward to showcasing that.”
In 2026, the host cities were Randers, Ringkøbing, Middelfart, Helsingør, and Copenhagen/Frederiksberg. This year, Denmark can expect new cities other than Silkeborg to join the Royal Run host club, with a new host city scheduled to be announced every day this week.
The Royal Run offers three distances to run, including 1.6 kilometers (also known as one mile), five kilometers, and ten kilometers.
The event first took place in 2018, when the then Crown Prince turned 50 years old. Since then, it has been held every year on Whit Monday.
Last year, a record 112,450 runners participated.

Russia re-opening Soviet-era military bases in Arctic, Kallas says
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
10:04:00 UTC
19:04:00 KST

Russia re-opening Soviet-era military bases in Arctic, Kallas says
EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kaja Kallas said this while speaking to journalists ahead of the European Arctic Summit in Finland on Monday, Ukrinform reports.
She noted that Russia is “opening ex-Soviet military bases, doing the missile testing here, in the Far North, showing clearly that this is a very important area.”
Kallas added that climate change is opening up new maritime routes that are becoming “increasingly important for the rest of the world.”
“The increasing power competition is truly unique here,” the EU High Representative stressed.
She separately noted that security and the environment are interconnected in certain respects, as Russia’s shadow fleet, among other threats it poses, is an “ecological bomb.”
As reported by Ukrinform, Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo invited a group of EU leaders to the European Arctic Summit in Rovaniemi on September 13–14.
The summit is attended by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal, Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs, Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda, Romanian President Nicușor Dan, and French Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs Jean-Noël Barrot.
Also attending are European Council President António Costa, EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kaja Kallas, and European Commissioner for International Partnerships Jozef Síkela.

Record number of schools opt out of PISA study
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
10:03:53 UTC
19:03:53 KST

Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen of the Social Democrats said Monday that she is “quite optimistic” Denmark, Greenland and the USA can reach an agreement on security and defense in Greenland.
Frederiksen spoke at a news conference in Finland, where she attended a European summit focused on security in the Arctic.
“We have agreed to start a high-level working group on closer cooperation on security and defense, also in Greenland,” Frederiksen said.
“As long as the working group between Greenland, Denmark, and the USA continues its work, it is too early to draw a conclusion. But I am quite optimistic that we will succeed in finding a way,” she said.
Frederiksen visited Greenland last week with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.
Denmark is among 10 NATO countries conducting a joint military exercise in Greenland. The exercise is intended to show that Denmark and NATO are protecting Greenland and the Arctic.
US President Donald Trump has criticized Denmark for not doing enough to protect Greenland from threats posed by Russia and China.
During the first weeks of September, 400 soldiers from 10 NATO countries are operating on land, at sea and in the air near Narsarsuaq and Kangerlussuaq. They are training to operate in Arctic conditions as part of NATO’s Arctic Sentry surveillance and deterrence mission.
“If one is to be able to operate in the Arctic, one has to train up here,” Søren Andersen, head of Denmark’s Arctic Command, told the Danish news agency Ritzau last week.
Andersen said the temporary Arctic Shield exercise is part of a long-term strategy for Greenland and the Arctic.
“For us, it is about helping to transform NATO’s northern flank into a hard target. Meaning all the way from Alaska across Canada, Greenland, and to the northern part of Norway,” he said.
Denmark and Greenland are also discussing whether to give the USA greater access to Greenland. The New York Times reported in the spring, based on American sources, that the USA wants three bases in Greenland as part of a possible agreement. Narsarsuaq and Kangerlussuaq were reportedly among the possible locations.
Danish Defense Minister Jeppe Bruus of the Social Democrats declined to discuss the working group’s talks during a visit to Narsarsuaq last week.
“I cannot comment on that. What goes on in that working group, goes on in that working group,” Bruus told Ritzau.
Bruus said the government wants to extend the operating period of Narsarsuaq Airport by one year if it receives support from the Folketing, Denmark’s parliament.
“Initially, it is a one-year extension. That gives us the opportunity to extend the playing board,” Bruus said.
Chief of Defense Michael Hyldgaard said Narsarsuaq would be an obvious possible location for an American base because of its position in southern Greenland and its access to transatlantic routes, the Denmark Strait and the GIUK gap.
The GIUK gap is the sea area between Greenland, Iceland and the United Kingdom. It is an important military passage where NATO can monitor and block Russian submarines moving toward the Atlantic.
The USA previously operated a military base in Narsarsuaq from July 1941 to November 1958.

Notorious fugitive Dutch arms dealer dies in South Africa
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
10:02:20 UTC
19:02:20 KST

Notorious fugitive Dutch arms dealer dies in South Africa
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
A timber merchant turned arms dealer, one of the Netherlands’ most infamous international fugitives, has died peacefully in South Africa after evading justice for years.
Guus Kouwenhoven, who facilitated weapons shipments to the Liberian dictator Charles Taylor in the early 2000s, was sentenced in absentia to 19 years for illegal arms smuggling and complicity in war crimes in 2017.
Despite being arrested in Cape Town, he was released on bail and avoided extradition, living a life of luxury, until his death last week.
Taylor, who was himself given a 50-year prison sentence in The Hague for crimes against humanity, waged civil wars in Liberia until 2003 that killed over 150,000 people. Kouwenhoven’s dealings with him were seen as instrumental to the fighting, which was notorious for its brutality and widespread use of child soldiers.
The Liberian press described Kouwenhoven as a reminder of the country’s violent past, referring to “blood timber”, and asked how someone could get away with turning the timber trade into a currency for war.
So far nothing has been said by Dutch justice minister David van Weel, despite the scale and notoriety of the case. Efforts to have him extradited were complicated and delayed even after South Africa revoked his visa, and his exuberant lifestyle reportedly went unhindered.
Given the recent efforts by Van Weel to push for Sierra Leone to extradite fugitive drugs baron Jos Leijdekkers – even by asking the EU to cut off development aid to the country until it hands him over – Kouwenhoven seems to have escaped proportional scrutiny in his final years, a Volkskrant column argued.

Merz wins respite in German municipal polls but tougher tests to come
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
10:01:37 UTC
19:01:37 KST

Europe's security trumps debates about my future, Germany's Merz says
ROVANIEMI, Finland, Sept 14 - Germany's under-fire Chancellor Friedrich Merz called on colleagues to look beyond debates about his political future on Monday, warning that the protection of Europe was entering a decisive phase in the coming weeks and months.
A year after taking office, Merz's position and his reform programme have come under pressure as his conservatives were trounced by the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) in a state election last week.
In an increasingly polarized political system, Merz, whose personal approval ratings have sunk to record lows, has been one of the main targets of voter ire over the cost of living, pensions and economic insecurity.
He won some respite over the weekend as his CDU conservatives topped municipal elections in the state of Lower Saxony, but will face a sterner test in two more state elections on Sunday. The AfD is set to top a poll in the eastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, while the state of Berlin also goes to the polls.
"Germany is so closely linked with the destiny of the European continent that we cannot decouple foreign security policy from what we are debating at home," Merz said, when asked about his position at an Arctic summit in Finland.
"That's the reason why I'm trying to convince my colleagues, my friends, my political party, the parliamentary group, that this is important, much more important than some of the domestic debates we actually have."
The AfD has called for a 180-degree turn on Germany's policy towards Russia, urging Berlin to restore ties with Moscow, regain access to Russia's abundant cheap energy resources and halt aid for Ukraine.
Germany has been Ukraine's biggest donor in Europe since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. Merz said he would not "go back one centimetre" on Berlin's policy.
"I know the arguments, I see the debate, I see the reservations we are seeing in parts of the country," he said. But he cautioned that if Russia prevailed, it would have "unprecedented consequences for all of us, including Germany."
MERZ'S PARTY WINS MUNICIPAL POLLS
Merz gained some relief after the CDU won 27.2% of the vote in municipal elections in the northwestern state of Lower Saxony at the weekend, with its coalition ally the Social Democrats on 24.6%, while the AfD climbed to third place with 15.9%.
The CDU's leader in the state, which is home to car firm Volkswagen and steelmaker Salzgitter among others, welcomed the result but called for change.
"I believe a political shift is needed in Berlin. We need to ease the burden on people. Energy prices are too high and housing costs are too high," Sebastian Lechner said in Hanover, according to Die Zeit newspaper.
"We, too, have sensed the dissatisfaction with Berlin."
Last week, the AfD came within touching distance of winning the election in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt outright and could yet form a government there, the first time a far-right party would do so in postwar Germany.
The results put the focus on whether Merz is now an electoral liability, and also whether he will be forced to change course on a reform programme that he says will revive sluggish growth in Europe's largest economy.
A poll by INSA over the weekend said 78% of people do not think Merz should be chancellor. Among his own party, 58% of voters no longer want Merz in charge, with 36% still backing him.
Clara von Nathusius, the treasurer of the CDU's youth wing, said the CDU had a credibility problem.
"It doesn't hinge solely on Friedrich Merz, though it does play a part," she told the ARD broadcaster. "And that is why, unfortunately, I believe no more elections can be won with this chancellor." REUTERS

Chinese dining chain drops ‘Stir-Fried Pork King’ title amid award scandal
‘Nowadays, everyone seems to be a master or an expert. These titles no longer carry the same weight,’ says a commenter
A Hunan restaurant brand from China has become a sensation in the US, yet faces scrutiny at home regarding its once-esteemed title of “Stir-Fried Pork King.”
Founded in 2003, Chef Fei has evolved into one of China’s most recognisable Hunan restaurant chains, celebrated for its fiery flavours and signature stir-fried pork dish.
The brand now operates over 200 outlets nationwide and reports having served more than 100 million customers in China by 2025.
On August 29, Chef Fei launched its first US outlet in San Diego, California. For many diners, the allure extended beyond a mere plate of chilli pork; it embodied the cultural experience that accompanied it.

Once upon a screen: explosive paradox
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-14
10:01:00 UTC
19:01:00 KST

‘What do you think this movie is about?’
In this video essay, the US filmmaker Kevin B Lee recalls the shock of seeing, as a young film buff, the raw, violent and widely acclaimed Vietnam War film Platoon (1986) with his family in a San Francisco cinema. Recording outside the building that once housed that cinema, he details his harrowing time in the theatre and the film’s reverberations in his life beyond the theatre’s walls, including how it stirred generational trauma in his family and racism at school. With his deceptively simple approach, Lee inverts and subverts Oliver Stone’s epic, crafting, on a shoestring budget, a profound and intensely personal meditation on memory. Lee’s video essay was published as part of ‘Once Upon a Screen’, a series of video essays about film viewing and childhood trauma, commissioned and curated by Ariel Avissar and Evelyn Kreutzer, for The Cine-Files journal of cinema studies, Issue 15.
